verdict.reasoning: Patient states she started to feel short of breath over the last hour while sitting and watching TV: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and confirmatory "This is while you're sitting watching tv?" "Yeah."

Patient reports a new cough since yesterday and that she has not brought anything up: "So I started with a cough yesterday" and "No, I haven't" when asked if she brought anything up, indicating non-productive cough.

Patient reports feeling stressed and her heart racing: "I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going" and doctor clarifies "you're feeling your heart more than normal?" "Yeah." This supports stress with palpitations.

Patient denies chest pain but notes soreness with deep breath: "And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?" "No." and "How about when you take a very deep breath in?" "I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore..."
Patient reports frequent coughs/colds and that the last similar illness was months ago: "You know, I get coughs and colds quite a lot, but probably good few months ago."
Patient reports a recent C-section four weeks ago: "I had a C section a few weeks ago." and when asked "how long ago was that?" she answers "Yeah. Four weeks."

Patient used codeine regularly after the C-section but stopped about a week ago: "They gave me some codeine." and "Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week."
Patient explicitly states an ibuprofen allergy: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though."
Patient reports maternal history of leg clots: "my mum's had clots in her legs before".
Same statement provides family history detail: "my mum's had clots in her legs before," which is family history of leg clots.

Patient has shortness of breath with recent C-section, and doctor expresses concern about clots including in chest/lungs: "Given that you've had a C section and you're short of breath... it might be worth you going into the hospital..." and "given that you've had a C section, some people can suffer with clots, and those can either be found in the legs or... your chest. So in your lungs." This supports a plan to rule out PE/DVT.

Doctor links elevated heart rate to shortness of breath and pain: "Good. So your heart is running slightly fast at the moment, which is probably because of your shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under."
Doctor advises immediate hospital evaluation: "it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further" and reiterates urgency: "what I would suggest is go fairly quickly".
Doctor advises avoiding further codeine use: "And if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being."
There is no explicit plan to monitor heart rate or shortness of breath over time; heart rate is measured once, and the plan is to go to hospital. No ongoing monitoring instruction is given.
Patient chooses to transport herself: doctor offers ambulance vs self-transport, and patient says "I'll go. I'll take myself." and later "I'll just take myself to the hospital."

Patient counts 30 beats over the timed interval, and doctor interprets this as slightly fast: "How many did you count?" "I counted 30." followed by "So your heart is running slightly fast at the moment..." The standard 15-second count implies 30 beats in 15 seconds, equating to an elevated rate.
